prompts.background: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: background illustration for an actual 16:9 television interface, NOT a mockup. Use the attached reference only for mood and illustration medium. Paint a rustic storybook reading nook opening onto a distant medieval castle, hazy mountains and a low warm sun. Fine pen-and-ink etching and watercolor on softly aged parchment, almost e-ink with muted moss, slate and ochre pigments. Quiet and luminous rather than dark or orange. Tree trunk and leafy branches frame the far left/top, old timber and one small lantern at far right; subtle books and tea at bottom left and sleeping cat at bottom right. The middle and lower-middle 80% must be calm pale warm parchment with barely perceptible scenery so separate interactive movie/app cards can be laid on it later. Landscape and castle occupy the upper quarter. Full bleed composition, straight on, no screen/device frame. Absolutely NO UI, cards, rectangles, icons, logos, letters, writing or watermark. High detail without visual noise. Wide 16:9 composition. Reference image is style guidance only; do not reproduce its movie posters or app logos.
prompts.posters: Create a square illustrated production atlas with exactly six portrait scenes in an exact 3-column by 2-row grid, equal-size cells, no gutters or margins. Each cell is 2:3 portrait. Old storybook ink etching with muted watercolor on ivory paper; rustic, tactile, quiet, near e-ink. In reading order: 1 a fully clothed young woman in a long green storybook dress sitting on a bayou bank looking at a small frog among fireflies; 2 a friendly panda holding a bamboo staff in autumn mountains with a distant pagoda; 3 a gray sled dog standing on a snowy forest ridge below the moon; 4 a mermaid wearing a modest green bodice sitting on a sea rock with a ship on the horizon; 5 a fully clothed solitary bell-ringer sitting on a cathedral gargoyle above old Paris with birds flying; 6 a friendly young long-neck dinosaur overlooking a fern-covered valley. These are six distinct self-contained original paintings, not a UI. No letters, writing, logos, titles, frames, watermark or text. Precise grid boundaries so the atlas can be displayed as six independent images.
